title: Shopper Tenure Kicker on Everyday Pay Card Cashback, Cartwise Shopper Payouts
content:
# Shopper recognition: the tenure kicker on card cashback

Long-serving shoppers on an Everyday Pay Card plan of Cartwise Shopper Payouts receive a tenure kicker with each statement payment. Tenure is read from the shopper's Cartwise Shopper Contractor Accounts record: the date the contractor account was first activated.

**Rule.** A tenure kicker is added outside the cap. A shopper whose contractor account was first activated 48 or more whole months ago gets 2.50; one activated 24 to 47 whole months ago gets 1.00; and any other shopper gets nothing.

## Kicker by whole months since first activation

| Whole months since the contractor account was first activated | Tenure kicker |
|---|---|
| 48 or more | 2.50 |
| 24 to 47 | 1.00 |
| 23 or fewer | none |

## Questions answered

**Which date is used when the contractor account was deactivated and later reactivated?** The date the account was first activated; tenure runs from that first activation.

**How are months counted?** In whole months up to the day of the payment. A shopper first activated 47 whole months and some days ago is in the 24 to 47 band and receives 1.00; on reaching 48 whole months the kicker is 2.50.

**Is the kicker limited by the monthly cashback cap?** No. It is added outside the cap, and it does not count toward whether a statement payment is owed.

## Illustration (hypothetical dates)

A shopper first activated on 10 March four years before the payment date of 10 March has 48 whole months and receives 2.50; on 9 March of that year the count is 47 whole months and the kicker is 1.00.
